headline: Poverty Incidence Among Filipinos Falls to 9.7% in 2025, PSA Reports
seoTitle: Philippine Poverty Incidence Falls to 9.7% in 2025 | FMB News
seoDescription: PSA reported that 9.7% of Filipinos were classified as poor in 2025, while poverty incidence among families fell to 6.4%, both reaching single-digit levels.
deck: Official 2025 poverty statistics show 9.7% of Filipinos were below the poverty threshold, while the rate among families fell to 6.4%.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that poverty incidence among individuals fell to 9.7% in 2025, equivalent to about 11.08 million Filipinos classified as poor under the official poverty threshold.
Poverty incidence among families fell to 6.4%, equivalent to about 1.90 million poor families. PSA said this was the first time the family poverty rate had fallen to a single-digit level.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The figures come from the 2025 Family Income and Expenditure Survey, conducted in July 2025 and January 2026. PSA said mean annual per-capita income grew faster than the poverty threshold between 2023 and 2025, helping push more households above the official line.

The approved FMB News brief characterized 9.7% as the country's record-low national poverty rate. FMB News is using PSA's more precise distinction between individual poverty incidence at 9.7% and family poverty incidence at 6.4%.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A lower poverty incidence suggests more households are earning enough to cover the minimum food and non-food needs represented by the official poverty threshold. The result also gives policymakers a clearer benchmark for judging whether growth, wage gains and social-protection programs are reaching lower-income households.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the PSA's regional and sectoral poverty tables for differences across provinces and population groups, as well as inflation, employment and income trends that could either reinforce or reverse the improvement.
